explanation: I searched Mathlib/NumberTheory/DiophantineApproximation/Basic.lean, where `Real.convergent` is defined, and ContinuedFractions.lean. They contain only convergent_zero, convergent_succ, convergent_of_zero, convergent_of_int, exists_rat_eq_convergent(') and convs_eq_convergent. None of these says anything about denominators growing. I also grepped Mathlib/Algebra/ContinuedFractions for `Tendsto`. The only hit is that the convergents `(of v).convs` tend to `v` (`𝓝 v`). There is no statement that the denominators go to infinity, and no Fibonacci lower bound on `(ξ.convergent n).den`. The proof relies on the library's own lemma `fib_succ_le_den_convergent`.
